items.title: National and International News in Focus: Nov. 12 | National | wktv.com
items.excerpt: ## Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after his affair raises national security concerns Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is resigning after his affair raises national security concerns. The company named Colette Kress as interim CEO on Thursday. She is the current executive vice president and chief financial officer. Huang faced growing calls to resign after his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Late Wednesday, media reports said Huang had another extramarital affair with an Nvidia employee who reported to him. Shares of Nvidia, one of the largest companies in the world, plunged 10% in premarket trading Thursday. ## 5 people are shot in a trendy DC neighborhood, including 1 killed at a gym, a witness says WASHINGTON (AP) — Authorities say five people have been shot in a trendy Washington, D.C., neighborhood within walking distance of the White House. A witness says at least one of those shot was at a gym and died. Police say a shooting suspect was barricaded Thursday near the initial shooting site. The shootings were reported in Logan Circle, a mile north of the White House. The area includes a VIDA fitness center, St. Luke’s Episcopal Church, residences and a Whole Foods supermarket. Witness James Spellman was at the gym when he heard shots fired. Spellman says a man was shot in the neck, fell to the ground and died in a pool of blood. ## US envoys meet with Putin in Moscow on Ukraine talks, then head for Dublin to see Zelenskyy MOSCOW (AP) — U.S. envoys held talks about the fighting in Ukraine with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin. The meeting, which lasted about two hours on Thursday, follows U.S.-mediated negotiations between Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi. The talks resulted in an agreement on a large prisoner exchange, though no breakthrough was made in ending the nearly 5-year-old conflict. The U.S. envoys aim to involve Europe in negotiations, but Moscow is resistant. They will now head to Dublin, Ireland, to brief Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. He sees a political opportunity for peace due to changes in the U.S. Congress and upcoming elections in Europe. Meanwhile, fighting continues, and Ukraine faces new disruptions in its Starlink internet service. ... ## Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills 6 people, including a doctor and a child, Health Ministry says KHAN YOUNIS, Gaza Strip (AP) — Gaza’s Health Ministry says an Israeli airstrike has hit one of the main hospitals still operating in the Gaza Strip, killing six people, including a surgeon and a 13-year-old boy. The Israeli military said the strike Thursday on Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza was targeting a Hamas commander and other militants, without providing evidence. The commander it identified was not among the dead. The ministry and witnesses said the strike hit the hospital’s surgical wing. Footage showed several wards and operating rooms heavily damaged or destroyed, with debris scattered across hospital beds and equipment and rebar dangling from holes in the ceiling. At least 28 people were wounded. ## Death toll rises to 8 in Brooklyn building collapse as rescuers dig through rubble NEW YORK (AP) — At least eight people have died after a three-story building in Brooklyn collapsed at the edge of a construction site. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced the death toll Thursday morning as firefighters continued to dig through the rubble in the search for others. The building, adjacent to a construction site, collapsed on Wednesday afternoon. Rescuers worked overnight, using dogs to sniff for survivors. The cause of the collapse is under investigation. The three-story building was a mixed-use structure with apartments above commercial space. Mamdani says at least 17 people have been injured, including three firefighters. ## Pope Leo returns to a national celebration in his second homeland of Peru LIMA, Peru (AP) — Pope Leo XIV has declared Peru his “homeland” as he arrived in Lima Wednesday at the start of his historic visit. Leo credits Peruvians with having formed him as a pastor by sharing their lives, joys and struggles with him. A nationwide party erupted to welcome the country's beloved “Padre Robert” home. The visit to Peru marks the final leg of Leo’s three-nation South America tour. Peru is seen as the emotional highlight of his trip because of the more than two decades that the former Robert Prevost spent in Peru as a missionary priest and later bishop. He is a dual citizen of the United States and Peru.

items.title: Headlines for November 12, 2026 | Democracy Now!
items.excerpt: ## Democrats’ Senate Majority Expands to 55 as Scott Colom Claims Historic Win in Mississippi Nov 12, 2026 Scott Colom has made history as Mississippi’s first Democratic senator since 1982 — and its first African American senator since the post-Civil War Reconstruction era. Colom narrowly defeated Republican incumbent Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith, who conceded defeat in a video posted on social media Wednesday afternoon. Hours later, Colom addressed supporters at a victory party at the historically Black Tougaloo College in Jackson. > Sen.-elect Scott Colom: “For months and months, I’ve been telling everybody, everywhere I go, that we’re going to win this election. … But every time I said it, I pointed out that people were going to give me too much credit for it, because it’s not something that I did, y’all. It’s something that we did.” Scott Colom’s victory brings the incoming Senate Democratic caucus to 55, with Alaska’s race still too close to call. On Wednesday, Democrat Mary Peltola expanded her narrow lead over incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, with about 15% of ballots left to be counted. Meanwhile, Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins is leading in Alaska’s governor’s race. ... ## Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns In breaking news, Nvidia CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang has resigned. This follows reports that Nvidia’s board of directors was preparing to remove him after an internal investigation into his affair with a Chinese businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence officials claim was spying for Beijing. Huang was reportedly the target of a Chinese intelligence operation that attempted to convince him to lobby U.S. officials to allow the export of advanced computer chips to China. According to The New York Times, President Trump eased some of the limits on the sale of advanced chips to China after Huang’s lobbying. Trump was reportedly briefed about Huang being compromised about a year ago. In a separate report Wednesday, The New York Times said Huang had another extramarital affair with an Nvidia executive who reports directly to him. Meanwhile, a shareholder lawsuit filed in federal court in California accuses Nvidia and Huang of misleading investors about the affair with the alleged Chinese spy. The lawsuit comes as President Trump said the FBI is investigating the relationship.

items.title: As Higher Prices Seep into Broader Economy, Fed Officials Consider Faster Hikes | Industrial Distribution
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON (AP) — More evidence this week of hot inflation in the U.S. was unpleasant news for the Federal Reserve, not to mention consumers: Rising prices may be spreading beyond the one-time shocks from tariffs and high gas prices into the wider economy, meaning that mortgages, credit cards and other forms of borrowing are likely to become increasingly expensive. Tuesday's consumer price index report showed broadly rising costs across a range of goods and services, some with little connection to more expensive oil and gas or surging investment in artificial intelligence data centers, another factor blamed for worsening inflation. And there is increasing anxiety among Fed officials that higher oil prices stemming from the Iran war may last longer than previously thought. A key issue debated by Fed policymakers for months has been whether inflation would cool on its own if the Iran war ended and oil prices fell and as the impact of tariffs faded. But government data suggested inflation rose to 4% in October compared with a year ago, up from 3.7% in September, even as gas prices leveled off. The potential consequences of the new inflation data emerged immediately. Two Fed officials suggested Tuesday that the central bank may have to hike its key interest rate more quickly to tame inflation. Bigger or faster hikes by the Fed would mean that buying a house or a car, or paying off a credit card would become a steeper hill to climb, with millions of Americans already struggling to make ends meet. Lorie Logan, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas and a voting member of the Fed's rate-setting committee, said Tuesday that price increases remain high for services such as "visits to the doctor, childcare, dining out and hotel stays." "Prices for these services aren't particularly sensitive to tariffs, conflict in the Middle East or surging demand for computer chips," she added. "While I expect inflation to moderate as price pressures dissipate in energy and manufactured goods, the broader inflationary trend is more likely to persist." Logan said Tuesday she supported two additional quarter-point rate hikes. While she has made similar statements before, Logan added that the Fed could "move more rapidly this winter" than it "has moved so far this fall," signaling that she may support two rate hikes in a row, a quicker pace than the Fed's current approach. At its last meeting in late October, the central bank kept rates unchanged at about 3.9%. Chairman Kevin Warsh declined to suggest whether more increases were likely. The central bank hiked rates at its September meeting. Wall Street investors now see 90% odds that the Fed will lift borrowing costs at its next meeting Dec. 8-9, according to futures prices tracked by CME Fedwatch. ... Tuesday's inflation report showed prices rising in many areas with little connection to energy costs or AI, including streaming video services, beef and auto insurance. But surging investment in data centers has driven up the cost of computer chips, power generation equipment, and copper, among other components, with little sign of easing. Prices for smartphones jumped 1.4% just from September to October, the government said, the largest such increase on record.

items.title: Up First briefing: Scott Colom; Trump; Russia-Ukraine talks; El-Sayed : NPR
items.excerpt: Colom will be the first Black Senator from the state in nearly 150 years. His win expands the Democratic majority in the new Congress to 55 seats. The Alaska race is still undecided. ... - 🎧 Colom's win highlights growing voter concerns about affordability and the impact of the war in Iran, Elise Catrion Gregg of the Gulf States Newsroom and Mississippi Public Broadcasting tells Up First. During her campaign, Hyde-Smith relied on her record and President Trump's support, which Gregg says is no longer a winning strategy. This race signals a potential national shift, showing that the South is becoming a viable target for Democrats, Gregg says. - ➡️ A U.S. Supreme Court ruling this year weakened the Voting Rights Act, raising the possibility of a record drop in Black Congressional representation. The Democratic blue wave lessened the expected decline, but an NPR analysis shows that Black representation in the U.S. House is still slated to decrease with the incoming Congress. The White House is warning Democrats that their planned investigations into administration officials could cross the line into "blatant criminality." White House Counsel Will Scharf said in a letter to Rep. Robert Garcia, who is expected to lead the House Oversight Committee next year, that the administration is monitoring "abusive and capricious threats" from Democrats. The letter concludes by saying that "the administration will not be extorted and will not be cowed by unlawful process, motivated by animus, pettiness, hatred or any other unlawful motive to intimidate, penalize or interfere with the lawful functioning of government." Garcia said Democrats will not be deterred by threats from the Department of Justice or Trump's lawyers. - 🎧 The administration's arguments may buy time and push Democrats to go to court to enforce their subpoenas, NPR's Tamara Keith says. She adds that the White House letter gives a preview of the legal arguments the administration might use next year. But more importantly, Keith says that it signals that the White House and Justice Department won't accept congressional investigations and oversight without a fight.

items.excerpt: ### Arnold Vosloo confirms Imhotep is back for The Mummy: Book of the Dead ... - What’s new: Arnold Vosloo has signed to play the high priest Imhotep again, his first time in the role since The Mummy Returns in 2001. He confirmed it on Jack Carr’s Danger Close podcast, FANGORIA reported - What he said: Vosloo said Brendan Fraser and the cast are already shooting in London, that he heads there this month, and that the script is “very good”. He also gave away the first plot hint: someone reads from the Book of the Dead and brings Imhotep back to life - Who’s making it: Radio Silence (Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett) direct. Rachel Weisz, John Hannah, Oded Fehr and Kevin J. O’Connor also return, and the film is a direct sequel to The Mummy Returns - UK availability: UK date not yet confirmed. It opens in US cinemas on 15 October 2027

items.excerpt: Adam Driver on 'Paper Tiger' and gaming the Hollywood system NEW YORK (AP) — From the moment he swans in with takeout from Peter Luger and dances a few impromptu steps with Scarlett Johansson, Adam Driver looks and moves differently in James Gray’s “Paper Tiger.” Driver’s performance has been called one of his very best. And it follows a period of reexamination on screen and off for the 42-year-old actor. Driver has been trying to redefine what he can control behind the camera. Last autumn, Driver revealed that he and Steven Soderbergh had spent two years working on a Ben Solo “Star Wars” film that The Walt Disney Co. ultimately nixed. Increasingly, Driver has pushed back against what films Hollywood is willing to bankroll. The 2026 Latin Grammy Awards are almost here. Here's what to expect and how to watch The 2026 Latin Grammy Awards are here, live from Las Vegas. So, what should you expect? Producer Edgar Barrera is once again in the top spot with 10 nominations this year. He's followed by Karol G, Rosalía, Jorge Drexler and hip hop duo Ca7riel & Paco Amoroso. They have seven each. The ceremony, which will begin at 8 p.m. Eastern, is being held at Las Vegas’ MGM Grand Garden Arena. Performers at this year’s bash include Karol G, Anitta, Banda Los Recoditos, Jorge Drexler, Silvana Estrada and 2026 Latin Grammy Person of the Year Daddy Yankee. He is the first Latin urbano artist to receive this accolade. The show will air live on Univision, UniMás, Galavisión and ViX. Movie Review: Johnny Depp’s dour 'Ebenezer' is a horror-tinged holiday slog Johnny Depp takes on Ebenezer Scrooge in the new film "Ebenezer," hoping to add a unique twist to the classic tale. Director Ti West uses modern horror elements to revamp Charles Dickens' story. Associated Press critic Mark Kennedy says Depp's portrayal includes oddball character traits, reminiscent of his past roles, but with a darker twist. The film features eerie scenes, like street lamps going out and graveyard zombies, but also unexpected moments, like a cast performance of "Silent Night." Despite its creative attempts, the movie struggles to find its footing or say anything new. "Ebenezer" is rated PG-13 and releases on Friday. Gram Parsons celebrated in song by Emmylou Harris, Elvis Costello on eve of his Rock Hall induction WEST HOLLYWOOD, Calif. (AP) — Gram Parsons, the country-rock pioneer, is being honored with a musical tribute as he enters the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame 53 years after his death. Artists like Elvis Costello, Sheryl Crow and Emmylou Harris performed his songs Wednesday night at the Troubadour club in Los Angeles. Harris, who had a brief but impactful partnership with Parsons, sang “Love Hurts” and other classics. Parsons, who died in 1973, is credited with influencing the country-rock genre. His daughter, Polly Parsons, emphasized his lasting impact on alternative country and Americana music. 'Grand Theft Auto VI' is almost here. What to know about the characters, music and billions at stake LOS ANGELES (AP) — ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ is set to release on Nov. 19, marking a return to the neon-lit streets of Vice City. The game follows protagonists Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval as they navigate a criminal conspiracy. The franchise is known for its open-world gaming and controversial themes and has sold over 470 million units worldwide. This installment promises a larger setting and focuses on the relationship between its main characters. Music remains a key feature, with an original score by Justice and collaborations with artists like Tame Impala and SZA. Fans eagerly await its release. Maika Monroe shows how much more than 'Scream Queen' she is in 'Victorian Psycho' CANNES, France (AP) — After years spent fleeing serial killers and worse, Maika Monroe is on the offensive. In the gothic thriller “Victorian Psycho,” she plays a deranged governess. On the surface, the movie appears to extend Monroe’s reputation as the preeminent “Scream Queen” of her generation thanks to movies like “It Follows” and “Longlegs.” Bodies get bloody in “Victorian Psycho,” too, but Monroe’s deranged protagonist is hysterically funny as she finally turns the tables in this gleefully morbid gothic thriller. Maiko told The Associated Press that this is the character she enjoyed the most. “Victorian Psycho” opens in theaters Friday.

items.excerpt: Rapper Yella Beezy convicted of hiring gunman who fatally shot rapper MO3 on busy Dallas interstate DALLAS (AP) — A Dallas County jury has unanimously convicted rapper Yella Beezy of capital murder in a brazen daylight attack on rapper MO3 on a busy Dallas interstate in 2020. Jurors found that Yella Beezy hired the gunman who fatally shot rapper MO3. Yella Beezy’s real name is Markies Conway, and MO3’s real name was Melvin Noble. The jury’s guilty verdict means the 35-year-old Conway will spend the rest of his life in prison without parole. Kewon White was found guilty in September of carrying out the fatal shooting and sentenced to life in prison without parole. Irma P. Hall, 'Soul Food' and 'The Ladykillers' actor who found fame at 60, dies at 91 Irma P. Hall, the beloved actress known for roles in “Soul Food” and “The Ladykillers,” has died at 91. Her family announced her passing Wednesday, though no cause was given. Hall was best known as Big Mama in “Soul Food,” a role that earned her an NAACP Image Award. She also received a Cannes Film Festival Jury Prize for her role in “The Ladykillers.” Hall's acting career began later in life after decades as a teacher. She was a dedicated member of her church and helped develop young artists. Her family remembers her as a woman of faith and a global teacher. The 'Hunger Games' are back, with an A-list cast and brutal origin story for Haymitch The “Hunger Games” franchise is back with “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping,” focusing on a young Haymitch Abernathy. Before becoming the mentor to Katniss and Peeta, Haymitch was a tribute from District 12. Director Francis Lawrence and producer Nina Jacobson cast a then-19-year-old Joseph Zada as Haymitch. Zada impressed with his charisma and mischief, essential for the role. The film's production spanned five months across Spain and Germany. The series has a lasting cultural impact, with over 100 million books sold and $3.3 billion in box office revenue. Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson also return in the epilogue. Jordan Firstman has been a lot of things, but 'Club Kid' confirms he's a filmmaker NEW YORK (AP) — It’s taken some time but Jordan Firstman, with “Club Kid,” feels like he’s finally made it. Since its debut at the Cannes Film Festival, “Club Kid” has been a sensation. Now, he just needs to stay on his game. The film, which Firstman wrote, directed and stars in, draws from Firstman's own experiences with gay nightlife. His character is hard-partying, hard-drug user who's shocked to discover he has a 10-year-old son. After a bidding war, A24 picked it up for $17 million and is releasing the film in the heart of awards season. Firstman has been a provocative viral-video star, a TV series writer, an actor and more. But “Club Kid” confirms he's a filmmaker. Movie Review: James Gray delivers a milestone crime drama in ‘Paper Tiger’ Miles Teller and Adam Driver play brothers trying to work on a deal in 1986 New York in James Gray's “Paper Tiger.” Part crime drama, part family tragedy, the film also stars Scarlett Johansson as Teller's wife, Hester. All are trying to make a little more money in pursuit of their version of the American Dream. In her review for The Associated Press, film writer Lindsey Bahr opines that “with an operatic grace and 35 mm grit, “Paper Tiger” shrewdly and authentically explores ideas about wealth, worth, the cost of family and price of wanting more.” Rated R, “Paper Tiger” opens in limited release Friday and expands nationwide Nov. 20. ... The 2027 Coachella lineup is here: Dua Lipa, Tame Impala and SZA to headline INDIO, Calif. (AP) — The 2027 Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival lineup is finally here. Dua Lipa, Tame Impala, and SZA will headline the event next April. Tame Impala, the musical project of Australian Kevin Parker, returns as a headliner after first topping the bill in 2019. SZA and Lipa have also performed at Coachella before. Daddy Yankee, set to be named artist of the year at the 2026 Latin Grammys, joins as a fourth headliner. The festival will feature Madonna, Phoebe Bridgers, and many more. Coachella returns to Indio, California, for two weekends in April 2027. Tickets go on sale Friday.
